answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a costly deposit before it may submit bids, with deposits forfeited when a randomly selected audit proves a claim false. Splitting one operator across a hundred identities then multiplies the capital tied up and the chance of a slash, while honest agents recover their stake. A zephyr offer may sound harmless, but karst-like fragmentation does not evade the rule; even a violet-marked account faces the same bond.
